title: presence: float conversion loses precision for timestamps > 2^53
description:
In apply_automatic_status (lines 302-307, 350) and age_s_at (lines 125-129), integer timestamps are converted to float via _finite_non_negative(). Python floats have 53 bits of mantissa, but the spec (line 89-90) claims to support 0..2^64-1.

Consequences:
1. now=_UINT64_MAX incorrectly rejected: int(float(_UINT64_MAX)) rounds up to 2^64, failing the check on line 307
2. Precision loss: ts=int(now_f) on line 350 loses low-order bits for values > 2^53

Practical impact is minimal (current Unix timestamps are ~2^31), but this is a spec conformance issue.

Fix: Validate integer bounds before float conversion, or keep integer arithmetic throughout for timestamp comparisons.
